nodes.label: PersistentActor
nodes.rationale: Three methods do the work: onCommand validates and decides what to persist (side effects go in afterPersist), onEvent is a pure state+event to state function replayed on recovery, initialState is the pre-event state. Commands are not processed until recovery completes.

nodes.label: DurableStateActor
nodes.rationale: persist(newState) overwrites the stored snapshot and preStart loads it back — no event log, no replay. Durable-state stores carry a revision counter, so concurrent writes raise DurableStateConcurrencyError.

nodes.label: Event sourcing model
nodes.rationale: Persist a log of every state-changing fact. Wins when history matters (audit, compliance, 'how did we get here'), when state is large but changes are small, when projections are wanted, and when schema evolution is a long game — event types migrate independently of current state.

nodes.label: Durable state model
nodes.rationale: Persist a single current value, overwritten on each update. Wins when history is not useful and the state is small and simple enough that rewriting the whole thing per change is fine. Many production systems mix both models.

nodes.label: Backend matrix
nodes.rationale: Twelve rows crossing journal / durable state / snapshot store / indexed tag query / runtimes. CockroachDB and YugabyteDB are not separate backends but Postgres-wire servers the Postgres stores serve unchanged; Cassandra has no durable-state store and object storage has no journal. 'Indexed tag query' means currentEventsByTag can be pushed down to storage — the others scan and refine in memory, correct either way but bounded in cost only where there is an index.

nodes.label: Snapshots
nodes.rationale: Cut the replay window: load the latest snapshot, then replay only events after its seqNr. Pick the interval from the event rate and the acceptable startup time.

nodes.label: Projections / ProjectionActor
nodes.rationale: Decouples writes from reads: the projection consumes tagged events in order and persists its own offset so a restart resumes correctly. A throwing handler blocks every event behind it because the cursor only advances on success, which recoveryStrategy bounds — retry with backoff then stop, or skip to the dead-letter stream.

nodes.label: Journal.read replay contract
nodes.rationale: Events must come back ascending by sequence number, contiguous, and inside the requested window; delete compacts a prefix, never a hole in the middle. So a gap can only mean a defect — a missing ORDER BY, a half-written append, a store someone else can write — and replay raises JournalIntegrityError instead of folding it.

nodes.label: Tagged JSON tree payload format
nodes.rationale: Every backend stores payloads in the same tagged JSON tree format, so Date / Map / Set / bigint / Uint8Array round-trip everywhere and an event stream means the same thing on any store.

hyperedges.label: Optimistic-concurrency backstops across the journal backends
